record.title: microduck-robot-hat-pcb
record.why: MEASURED 2026-09-02 (lane T): the shelf's own check FAILed this folder for declaring ZERO interfaces, and that is settled — cad/interfaces.json now declares four MEASURED anchors read off Pollen's elec_rpi_robot_hat_pcb.stl by cecad.meshfeatures.cylinders at 0.0000 mm fit residual and 355.0 deg cover, frozen in out/laneT/features/elec_rpi_robot_hat_pcb.json: 'mount_holes' (4 x Ø2.7000 on a 58.0000 x 23.0000 mm rectangle — the Raspberry Pi HAT pitch), 'header_2x20' (40 x Ø1.0200 on a 2.5400 mm grid, rows y +-1.2700, columns x 4.8700..53.1300, plus 2 x Ø2.0000 anchors), 'peripheral_connectors' (14 x Ø0.9500 in two 2.5000 mm-pitch blocks) and 'board_outline' (65.0250 x 30.0250 x 0.8400 mm). WHAT IS STILL MISSING, named: (1) the board's modelled thickness is 0.8400 mm and a Raspberry Pi HAT is fabricated at 1.6000 mm — either the mesh is a simplified placeholder or this board really is 0.84 mm, and that matters for the head stack-up; (2) WHICH connectors the 14 x Ø0.9500 holes are cannot be read off a mesh, which carries no silkscreen and no refdes. What settles both: the board file the PCB lane is producing in electronics/robot-hat/, or a photograph of a real Robot HAT. This is one of the three custom PCBs COMPARISON.html finding 6 names as having no published design.
record.origin_why: the geometry is Pollen Robotics' own published sim asset (reference/pollen-microduck-rl/assets/elec_rpi_robot_hat_pcb.stl), measured but not designed here; CC BY-SA-NC 4.0 per the pollen-robotics/microduck_rl README.
